findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

1) An employee was observed to handle their phone and not wash their hands prior to resuming food service. 2) An employee was observed to change gloves without hand washing. 3) An employee was observed to touch their clothing and head without hand washing. 4) An employee was observed to have a drink and not wash their hands prior to resuming food service. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to refresh hand washing procedures (including when to wash hands) with all staff to prevent future issues. Wash hands whenever they are contaminated and prior to handling foods/food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The salad prep cooler was observed with internal temperatures for lettuce, cheeses and house made mayo based sauces are observed in the 51F-52F range. The foods were discarded to correct and the cooler should be monitored moving forward to ensure effective cold holding is taking place.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The egg wash (milk and eggs) on the prep line were observed holding around 60F in its ice bath. The ice is only touching the bottom of the inner pan and the pans are located between the grill and the fryers. The current set up does not allow for ice to surround the egg wash with the current equipment. Education was conducted with the PIC and staff. The current egg wash was discarded and a new set up with a larger ice pan and an egg wash pan that allows for the ice to surround ice will be used moving forward. Ensure that the ice is maintained at a level around the food that is higher than the level of the food. Monitor the egg wash temperatures throughout use times to ensure that effective cold holding is maintained at all times.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. 

A pan of white sauce is observed in the right most prep cooler during the inspection. This pan came from a batch observed earlier in the inspection on a counter cooling and was observed at 60F-80F depending on where the internal temperature was observed. Education was conducted with the PIC. This equipment is not sufficient for cooling hot foods, especially while the cooler is in use for active food preparation. The pan was moved to the walk ins for rapid cooling. Stirring is also suggested because of the temperature gradient observed. Ensure that all foods are cooled effectively at all times in the facility moving forward.

750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:

Chef states that the cooler lids are regularly left open during the lunch and dinner rush. He stated the cooler lid was most likely opened around 11:00 AM. Facility was allowed to use the items in this cooler until 15:00, then discarded them. 3) Observed pasta (ravioli, angel hair, spaghetti) within the pasta prep cooler drawers to be out of temperature control (probed at 55-58F). Ensure that during rush periods that the PHFs within the coolers are not coming out of temperature due to the lids/drawers being constantly open. Any RTE, PHFs should be date marked with the day they were opened and discarded after 7 days of service. If they are frozen, then they should have the date they were prepared/open, date they were frozen, and date the item was thawed.

750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment:

750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:

750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.

750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:

750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:

750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly

findings.comment: 750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below. The second pasta cooler is holding food at between 43F and 45F.  The foods were just loaded into the coolers to prepare for lunch. Do not store stock in the units.  Over stock was removed to the walk in cooler. Cooler had been open and cleaned this morning. Provide coolers that function properly and hold product temperature.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F. Thermometers are missing or not functioning in the 2nd pasta cooler and the glass front wait staff cooler. provide thermometers in all cold holding units.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. No test kit provided for quat sanitizer. Provide test kit for quat sanitizer.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Sanitizer concentration in the dish machine was zero parts per million chlorine. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.
750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). The sanitizer concentration in the 3 part sink and sanitation buckets was zero parts per million of quaternary ammonia sanitizer. Use of the automatic sanitizer feeder was discontinued ant the sanitizer is being added by hand to provide the proper concentration of sanitizer in the third part of the sink.
Dish machine is being used for wash only and equipment is being sanitized in the third part of the sink.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. The following non food contact surfaces are soiled 1) top of  glass cooler, under netting at bar 2) vents on cooling units. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch. The cove in the closet with jackets is missing and the floor is soiled. Clean floor and repair cove.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents. The wall in the wait station area has a large hole in it. Repair the wall.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
(Repeat Violation)  Observed the white, plastic piece inside the ice machine to be soiled with possible mold accumulation.  Clean and sanitize this plastic piece inside the ice machine and do so often, to prevent mold growth.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the green wire shelving in the server area, where glasses are stored, to be soiled and inside the doors of the fryers, in the mechanical area, to have grease accumulation.  Clean the green shelves and the inside doors and mechanical area of the fryers.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
At next remodel of the facility, replace ceiling tiles over the bar, pizza prep area and oven, in server areas, and in all restrooms with tiles that are non-absorbant, smooth, and easily cleanable.  The current ceiling tiles are pitted, acoustic tiles, painted black, but do not need to be replaced until next remodel of facility.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750.280: Observed an ice cream scoop that had been used to be stored in a container of room temperature water by the chest freezer.  An ice cream scoop shall be stored clean and dry, in the ice cream with the handle extended up, or in a running dipper well.

750.280: Observed cheese graters that had been used to be stored soiled with pieces of grated cheese. An employee stated that the graters are washed once a day, but they need to be washed properly at least after lunch and after dinner service because there are pieces of potentially hazardous food (cheese) left on the grater.  The graters could also be stored in the cooler in between uses to minimize the growth of microorganisms. *Both violations were corrected during inspection*

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b: Observed the plastic piece inside the ice machine to have some mold growth.  Clean and sanitize this plastic piece inside the ice machine to remove the mold and do so often to prevent mold growth.

findings.comment: 750.1060: Observed a leak at the handsink closest to the back door and kitchen area.  Repair the leak at this sink.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed a large clear plastic container storing lettuce in the salad prep cooler to have a large crack in it.  Food contact surfaces shall be free from crevices and projections, so it is smooth and easily cleanable.  Discard the container or use it for something other than to store food products.
